title: A click on a control changes the screen
note: Clicks reach controls that do something visible: the route, the selection or the content changes.
intent: The first thing anyone does is click. If nothing responds, the page feels broken whatever else is true. Wire each navigation control to a real change a person can see: a different view, a selected tab, an expanded section, a filtered list. Reflect the current view in the address (hash or history) so back works and a reload lands where you were. Mark the active item (aria-current="page") and style it. Keep targets at least 40 px so they are easy to hit. The page counts navigations and visible reactions to input in state().ui.navigations and ui.reactions.

check.note: After the scripted clicks the address or the page changed: a navigation or a reaction was counted, or the page reports another view (a link to a separate HTML page starts its counters at zero).

port: One router module owns the current view; links are plain <a href="#/view"> so the browser does the history work, and the shell renders from the route.
